cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Helpful Culprit
cards.instruction: Hide that the problem is your fault while enthusiastically helping investigate it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll investigate the dead office plant. Please don't empty the pot; we need the liquid as it was.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You watered it with your coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll compare it with a fresh cup from the machine. A source is not a conclusion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You put six sugars in yours. The machine didn't do that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six in the comparison cup, then. Please label it correctly; I'd like one controlled sample before everyone decides who killed a fern.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sample preservation, A3 comparison and A5 controlled preparation are expert corrections used to hide A causal responsibility.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 coffee attribution causes A3 source comparison; B4 six sugars requires A5 matching composition.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 seek acknowledgement of A watering mistake through direct evidence while A remains an eager investigator.

heightening.evidence: A5 incorporates the incriminating personal addition as a test specification instead of admitting guilt.

specificity.evidence: A1 dead office plant and B2 coffee watering establish the whole immediate problem.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 label request and controlled sample are functional deflection, though the last clause is slightly full.

coach2.firstDefect: No essential confusion; A5 closing clause could be tighter in spoken delivery.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 turns B2 coffee into the proposed comparison source.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 identifies what differs between A3 machine coffee and the poured drink.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 incorporates B4 six sugars into the control while deferring blame.
